clue.text: Meeting extra-terrestrial in sport centre —- who'd believe it!

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letter of the word sport
in tells us the alien is put inside the phrase for nobody

parts.note: an exclamation that nobody would credit it: no one
ET is the film alien, short for extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: An alien turns up at the leisure centre, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who'd believe it!' is not a closing aside but part of the wordplay: the reply no one would.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-to-one is a private meeting between two people, such as a manager and an employee.

clue.text: Bring engagement ring and chalice in hollow cavity

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: in means the cup goes inside the emptied cavity
hollow means the word cavity is emptied, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: a chalice is a cup

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes an engagement ring and a goblet set into a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring engagement' reads oddly as a definition: occupying someone engages their attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy someone is to keep them engaged or busy, bringing engagement to their mind.

clue.text: Raise volume at end of scene?

definitions.text: Raise volume at end of scene?

indicators.note: in a down clue raise means the word for volume is read upwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book or volume

indicators.note: end of asks for the last letter of the word scene

explanation.surface: An actor turns up the loudness for a dramatic finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns TOME to EMOT, and 'end of' adds E, the last letter of 'scene'. Taken whole, the clue describes overacting.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to show feeling theatrically, as a ham actor raising his voice for the curtain does.

clue.text: Group in circulation following orders, after a fashion

parts.note: O is a blood group, and blood is what circulates in the body
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
sorts means orders or arranges

explanation.surface: A team on the move obeys its instructions, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group in circulation' reads like a team doing the rounds, but it is a blood group: O.
explanation.definitionFit: Of sorts is an idiom meaning of a rough or mediocre kind, so roughly after a fashion.

clue.text: Fuel bore used in marking plain

indicators.note: used in means the two pieces are put inside the word for marking

parts.note: noting is marking or observing
oil is a fuel
a pain is a bore, a nuisance

explanation.surface: An engineer drills a fuel bore while surveying flat country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' means unattractive, not flat land; 'Fuel bore' is two separate pieces, not a drilled hole.
explanation.definitionFit: No oil painting is a British idiom for someone unattractive, plain in looks.

clue.text: Keep going for new setter, perhaps

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a pup is a young dog, and a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A newly hired crossword setter is told to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is not a compiler but the dog breed; a new one is a pup.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up something is to support it and keep it going, as with a failing business.

clue.text: After accepting a little money, remains a model

indicators.note: After places the a at the end, following the rest
accepting means the coin is taken inside the word for remains

parts.note: a relic is something that remains from the past
p, a penny, is a small amount of money

explanation.surface: Once a small fee is paid, an old relic serves as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb but is the noun, an old relic.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy or scale model of something.

clue.text: By design, extra-large tablet rather violet round the edges

indicators.note: round the edges means the colour word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: purply means somewhat purple, rather violet in colour
OS is outsize, a clothing size bigger than large
E is ecstasy, a drug taken as a tablet

explanation.surface: A huge pill with a mauve rim is described as deliberate.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy, a drug taken as a tablet, is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Purposely means intentionally, so it matches by design, deliberately.

clue.text: Old man runs and trips over roots

parts.note: pa is father, informally one's old man
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: over means the word for trips is turned round

parts.note: spins are short trips, like a spin in the car

explanation.surface: A father jogs and stumbles over tree roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SPINS into SNIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are root vegetables, so they are examples of roots.

clue.text: Is showing off bottom a sign of age?

parts.note: to crow is to boast, so is showing off gives crows
the foot of something is its bottom, as of a page

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether flaunting one's backside betrays one's years.
explanation.definitionFit: Crow's feet are the fine wrinkles at the corner of the eye that come with getting older.

clue.text: Vehicle rumbles above, so one can't speak?

indicators.note: above, in a down clue, puts the rumbling word over the vehicle

parts.note: thunders means rumbles loudly
a truck is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A lorry rumbles overhead, drowning out conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thunderstruck means being so amazed that one is left speechless.

clue.text: Norm for serving men to feed one prunes

indicators.note: to feed means the soldiers are put into the word for norm

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
RE, the Royal Engineers, are men serving in the British Army

explanation.surface: Soldiers are told the standard rations include prunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one prunes' is a definition, a person or tool that pares, not fruit to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parer trims or cuts back, which is what someone who prunes does to a plant.

clue.text: Membrane's energy conserved by more than one

indicators.note: conserved by means the energy is kept inside the word for more than one

parts.note: plural means more than one
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A physics-flavoured remark about a membrane whose energy is preserved by many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Membrane's' is possessive because the answer is an adjective meaning of the membrane.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleural describes the pleura, the membrane around the lungs, so it stands for the possessive Membrane's.

clue.text: Representative of Scotland's crop of students?

parts.note: uni, short for university, is where students are
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A Scottish university harvest stands for the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'crop of students' as the university's corn: UNI + CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is Scotland's national animal and appears on its royal coat of arms.

clue.text: Be reconciled after brush with constitution

parts.note: a kiss can be a light brush of the lips
and means together with
your make-up is your constitution or nature

explanation.surface: A couple patch things up after a brush with the country's constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brush with' tempts as one phrase meaning an encounter; split it into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up after a quarrel with a kiss is the idiom for becoming friends again.

clue.text: Container from oven mounted on grate

parts.note: a kiln is an oven for firing pottery

indicators.note: mounted, in a down clue, means the word for on is turned upwards

parts.note: re means on, about, concerning
to jar is to grate on the ear or nerves

explanation.surface: An oven is set on top of a fire grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns RE to ER. A Kilner jar is a British brand of glass preserving jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kilner jar is a glass jar with a sealed lid used for preserving food, a type of container.

clue.text: One who made slow progress in French course?

definitions.text: One who made slow progress in French course?

parts.words: One who made slow progress in French course?
parts.note: a slow-moving creature cooked and served as a course at a French meal

explanation.surface: A struggling language student falls behind in French class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a dish in a meal, not a class; the slow mover is a snail on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French culinary name for an edible snail, a slow creature served as a dish.

clue.text: Second in farewell race — then extremely dodgy liver for six days

indicators.note: in tells us the brief moment goes inside the word for farewell

parts.note: so long is a way of saying goodbye
mo is a moment, a second
to run is to race

indicators.note: extremely asks for the first and last letters of the word dodgy

explanation.surface: A runner says goodbye mid-race, then a dodgy liver gives out within a week.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Solomon Grundy is born on Monday and dies on Saturday, buried on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme figure lives from his Monday birth to his Saturday death, six days of life.

clue.text: Crude poem had one shocked

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters of poem had are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: A vulgar verse has left one reader appalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocked' means having a shock of hair, not startled.
explanation.definitionFit: A mophead is a person with a thick shock of untidy hair, so someone shocked in that sense.

clue.text: Oriental city's Indian master baker?

definitions.meaning: a city in eastern China, now usually written Nanjing; 's here stands for is
a whimsical reading as king of naan, the Indian flatbread

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as NAN, the Indian bread, and KING, the master.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanking is the older spelling of Nanjing, a major city in eastern China.

clue.text: Fits well with text

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well
SMS is a text message

explanation.surface: Someone who is perfectly fine sends a text message.
explanation.definitionFit: Fits and spasms are both sudden involuntary attacks or convulsions.

clue.text: Helipad designed for theatre

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters of helipad being laid out anew

explanation.surface: Someone has drawn up plans for a helicopter landing pad on a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adelphi is a well-known theatre on the Strand in London's West End.

clue.text: Work on leather knots for garment

indicators.note: on here means the piece for work is added on after the others

parts.note: to tan is to make hide into leather, and tan is a leather colour
kt is the abbreviation for knot, the unit of speed at sea
op, short for opus, is a work of music

explanation.surface: Someone working with leather ties knots to make clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work on leather' looks like tanning, but that leaves nothing for OP; Work is the opus, placed after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless knitted pullover, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Hotel in resort something pivotal

indicators.note: in resort, read as re-sorted, means the letters of hotel are sorted again

explanation.surface: A hotel at a holiday spot is seen as central to its trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the holiday setting but means sort again.
explanation.definitionFit: A thole is a pin in a boat's gunwale that serves as the pivot for an oar.

clue.text: One serving America's greater interest jealous of Europe's leaders

indicators.note: leaders asks for the first letters of the five words before it

explanation.surface: An American official envies Europe's top people for their influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A GI is an enlisted American soldier, someone serving the United States in its army.

clue.text: Excess, I sense, not easy to shake off?

parts.note: a glut is an excess or surplus
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: Someone feels overwhelmed by a surplus they cannot get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutinous means sticky like glue, so a glutinous substance clings and is hard to remove.

clue.text: Abuse sort of winds around one

indicators.note: around means the trade winds wrap the letter for one

parts.note: the trade winds blow steadily towards the equator
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A forecaster grumbles about some kind of wind circling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts TRADE around I, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of abuse or criticism.

clue.text: After second lot of beer, head for resort

parts.note: a keg is a cask holding a quantity of beer
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: After a second round of drinks, someone sets off for the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not the verb but NESS, a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Skegness is a seaside holiday town on the Lincolnshire coast of England.
